# Resource: stripe_payment_intent

A customer payment. Set `status` to `succeeded` to confirm the intent with its `payment_method` and, when `capture_method` is `manual`, to capture it in the same apply; set it to `canceled` to cancel one that has not succeeded. Confirming with a card that needs a further action, or that is declined, leaves the intent where Stripe put it and fails the apply. Setting `payment_method` moves the intent to `requires_confirmation`; a test payment method such as `pm_card_visa`, which Stripe turns into a new one, stays in the state as configured. Stripe changes `amount`, `currency` and `setup_future_usage` only before the intent is confirmed (`requires_payment_method`, `requires_confirmation` or `requires_action`), `statement_descriptor_suffix` also while it is `requires_capture`, and `capture_method` only while it is `requires_payment_method` or `requires_confirmation`; it refuses such a change in any other status, and the apply fails. `description`, `metadata` and `receipt_email` still change once it has succeeded. `transfer_group` is sent on creation only: Stripe refuses to change a transfer group once set, so a plan that sets or changes it on an existing payment intent fails, and removing it from the configuration keeps the current value. The `client_secret` is sensitive.

~> A payment intent can move real money. In a live-mode Stripe account, creating or changing one, including setting its `status`, fails at plan time unless the provider sets `allow_live_money_movement = true`. Reading or importing one never does. The provider asks Stripe for the account's mode. See the Managing Test Data guide.

~> Stripe cannot delete a payment intent; set `status` to `canceled` to cancel one that has not succeeded. `terraform destroy`, and a change that would replace the payment intent, fail at plan time. To stop managing a payment intent, remove it from the state as [Removing from State](#removing-from-state) shows; it stays in the Stripe account.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "stripe_customer" "acme" {
  email = "billing@acme.example"
}

# A succeeded test payment: the intent is confirmed with Stripe's test card in the same apply.
resource "stripe_payment_intent" "order" {
  amount         = 2000
  currency       = "usd"
  customer       = stripe_customer.acme.id
  payment_method = "pm_card_visa"
  status         = "succeeded"

  automatic_payment_methods = {
    enabled         = true
    allow_redirects = "never"
  }
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are required:

* `amount` - (Required) Amount intended to be collected by this PaymentIntent. A positive integer representing how much to charge in the [smallest currency unit](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies#zero-decimal) (e.g., 100 cents to charge $1.00 or 100 to charge ¥100, a zero-decimal currency). The minimum amount is $0.50 US or [equivalent in charge currency](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies#minimum-and-maximum-charge-amounts). The amount value supports up to eight digits (e.g., a value of 99999999 for a USD charge of $999,999.99).
* `currency` - (Required) Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).

The following arguments are optional:

* `allowed_payment_method_types` - (Optional) The list of payment method types allowed for use with this payment. Stripe automatically returns compatible payment methods from this list in the `payment_method_types` field of the response, based on the other PaymentIntent parameters, such as `currency`, `amount`, and `customer`. Default: none.
* `amount_details` - (Optional) Provides industry-specific information about the amount. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value. See [`amount_details`](#amount_details) below.
* `application_fee_amount` - (Optional) The amount of the application fee (if any) that will be requested to be applied to the payment and transferred to the application owner's Stripe account. The amount of the application fee collected will be capped at the total amount captured. For more information, see the PaymentIntents [use case for connected accounts](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/connected-accounts). Default: none.
* `automatic_payment_methods` - (Optional) When you enable this parameter, this PaymentIntent accepts payment methods that you enable in the Dashboard and that are compatible with this PaymentIntent's other parameters. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value. See [`automatic_payment_methods`](#automatic_payment_methods) below.
* `capture_method` - (Optional) Controls when the funds will be captured from the customer's account. Possible values: `automatic`, `automatic_async`, `manual`. Default (Stripe): `automatic_async`. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `confirmation_method` - (Optional) Describes whether we can confirm this PaymentIntent automatically, or if it requires customer action to confirm the payment. Possible values: `automatic`, `manual`. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced. Default (Stripe): `automatic`. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `confirmation_token` - (Optional) ID of the ConfirmationToken used to confirm this PaymentIntent. If the provided ConfirmationToken contains properties that are also being provided in this request, such as `payment_method`, then the values in this request will take precedence. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced. Stripe refused it on a US account on create: "No such confirmationtoken: 'ctoken_...'".
* `customer` - (Optional) ID of the Customer this PaymentIntent belongs to, if one exists. Payment methods attached to other Customers cannot be used with this PaymentIntent. If [setup_future_usage](https://docs.stripe.com/api#payment_intent_object-setup_future_usage) is set and this PaymentIntent's payment method is not `card_present`, then the payment method attaches to the Customer after the PaymentIntent has been confirmed and any required actions from the user are complete. If the payment method is `card_present` and isn't a digital wallet, then a [generated_card](https://docs.stripe.com/api/charges/object#charge_object-payment_method_details-card_present-generated_card) payment method representing the card is created and attached to the Customer instead. Default: none.
* `customer_account` - (Optional) ID of the Account representing the customer that this PaymentIntent belongs to, if one exists. Payment methods attached to other Accounts cannot be used with this PaymentIntent. If [setup_future_usage](https://docs.stripe.com/api#payment_intent_object-setup_future_usage) is set and this PaymentIntent's payment method is not `card_present`, then the payment method attaches to the Account after the PaymentIntent has been confirmed and any required actions from the user are complete. If the payment method is `card_present` and isn't a digital wallet, then a [generated_card](https://docs.stripe.com/api/charges/object#charge_object-payment_method_details-card_present-generated_card) payment method representing the card is created and attached to the Account instead. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced. Stripe refused it on a US account on create and update: "The supplied ID is not a valid Customer. V2 Accounts must be configured as Customers before they can be used in the Customers API.". Default: none.
* `description` - (Optional) An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users. Default: none.
* `excluded_payment_method_types` - (Optional) The list of payment method types to exclude from use with this payment. Default: none.
* `hooks` - (Optional) Automations to be run during the PaymentIntent lifecycle. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value. See [`hooks`](#hooks) below.
* `mandate` - (Optional) ID of the mandate that's used for this payment. This parameter can only be used with [`confirm=true`](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_intents/create#create_payment_intent-confirm). Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced. Stripe refused it on a US account on create: "No such mandate: 'mandate_...'".
* `metadata` - (Optional) Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`. Default (Stripe): `{}`.
* `on_behalf_of` - (Optional) The Stripe account ID that these funds are intended for. Learn more about the [use case for connected accounts](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/connected-accounts). Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced. Default: none.
* `payment_details` - (Optional) Provides industry-specific information about the charge. See [`payment_details`](#payment_details) below.
* `payment_method` - (Optional) ID of the payment method (a PaymentMethod, Card, or [compatible Source](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-methods/transitioning#compatibility) object) to attach to this PaymentIntent. If you omit this parameter with `confirm=true`, `customer.default_source` attaches as this PaymentIntent's payment instrument to improve migration for users of the Charges API. We recommend that you explicitly provide the `payment_method` moving forward. If the payment method is attached to a Customer, you must also provide the ID of that Customer as the [customer](https://docs.stripe.com/api#create_payment_intent-customer) parameter of this PaymentIntent. Default (Stripe): none, or the method Stripe makes from `payment_method_data`, which this attribute does not hold.
* `payment_method_configuration` - (Optional) The ID of the [payment method configuration](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_method_configurations) to use with this PaymentIntent. Stripe does not return this value; the provider keeps it from configuration. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `payment_method_data` - (Optional) If provided, this hash will be used to create a PaymentMethod. The new PaymentMethod will appear in the [payment_method](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_intents/object#payment_intent_object-payment_method) property on the PaymentIntent. See [`payment_method_data`](#payment_method_data) below.
* `payment_method_options` - (Optional) Payment method-specific configuration for this PaymentIntent. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value. See [`payment_method_options`](#payment_method_options) below.
* `radar_options` - (Optional) Options to configure Radar. Learn more about [Radar Sessions](https://docs.stripe.com/radar/radar-session). Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced. See [`radar_options`](#radar_options) below.
* `receipt_email` - (Optional) Email address to send the receipt to. If you specify `receipt_email` for a payment in live mode, you send a receipt regardless of your [email settings](https://dashboard.stripe.com/account/emails). Default: none.
* `setup_future_usage` - (Optional) Indicates that you intend to make future payments with this PaymentIntent's payment method. If you provide a Customer with the PaymentIntent, you can use this parameter to [attach the payment method](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/save-during-payment) to the Customer after the PaymentIntent is confirmed and the customer completes any required actions. If you don't provide a Customer, you can still [attach](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_methods/attach) the payment method to a Customer after the transaction completes. If the payment method is `card_present` and isn't a digital wallet, Stripe creates and attaches a [generated_card](https://docs.stripe.com/api/charges/object#charge_object-payment_method_details-card_present-generated_card) payment method representing the card to the Customer instead. When processing card payments, Stripe uses `setup_future_usage` to help you comply with regional legislation and network rules, such as [SCA](https://docs.stripe.com/strong-customer-authentication). Possible values: `off_session`, `on_session`. Default: none.
* `shipping` - (Optional) Shipping information for this PaymentIntent. See [`shipping`](#shipping) below.
* `statement_descriptor` - (Optional) Text that appears on the customer's statement as the statement descriptor for a non-card charge. This value overrides the account's default statement descriptor. For information about requirements, including the 22-character limit, see [the Statement Descriptor docs](https://docs.stripe.com/get-started/account/statement-descriptors). Setting this value for a card charge returns an error. For card charges, set the [statement_descriptor_suffix](https://docs.stripe.com/get-started/account/statement-descriptors#dynamic) instead. Stripe takes it only beside a `statement_descriptor_suffix` that the same request sends or, on an update, that the intent already holds, as the conformance suite recorded with a card payment method and with none. Elsewhere Stripe refused it on a US account on create and update: "The statement_descriptor parameter is not supported for the payment_method_type `card`. To continue supporting payment_method_type `card`, please pass in `statement_descriptor_suffix` or remove the `statement_descriptor` parameter altogether. Please see https://support.stripe.com/questions/use-of-the-statement-descriptor-parameter-on-paymentintents-for-card-charges for additional details.". Default: none.
* `statement_descriptor_suffix` - (Optional) Provides information about a card charge. Concatenated to the account's [statement descriptor prefix](https://docs.stripe.com/get-started/account/statement-descriptors#static) to form the complete statement descriptor that appears on the customer's statement. Default: none.
* `status` - (Optional) Status of this PaymentIntent, one of `requires_payment_method`, `requires_confirmation`, `requires_action`, `processing`, `requires_capture`, `canceled`, or `succeeded`. Read more about each PaymentIntent [status](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/intents#intent-statuses). Possible values: `succeeded`, `canceled`. Removing it from the configuration stops sending it, and the next apply records the value Stripe holds.
* `transfer_data` - (Optional) The parameters that you can use to automatically create a Transfer. Learn more about the [use case for connected accounts](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/connected-accounts). See [`transfer_data`](#transfer_data) below.
* `transfer_group` - (Optional) A string that identifies the resulting payment as part of a group. Learn more about the [use case for connected accounts](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/separate-charges-and-transfers). Stripe refused it on a US account on update: "You cannot change `transfer_group` via API once it has been set.". Default: none. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.

<a id="amount_details"></a>
### `amount_details`

The `amount_details` attribute supports:

* `discount_amount` - (Optional) The total discount applied on the transaction represented in the [smallest currency unit](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies#zero-decimal). An integer greater than 0. This field is mutually exclusive with the `amount_details[line_items][#][discount_amount]` field. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `enforce_arithmetic_validation` - (Optional) Stripe does not return this value; the provider keeps it from configuration.
* `error` - (Read-Only) See [`amount_details.error`](#amount_details.error) below.
* `shipping` - (Optional) Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value. See [`amount_details.shipping`](#amount_details.shipping) below.
* `tax` - (Optional) Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value. See [`amount_details.tax`](#amount_details.tax) below.

<a id="amount_details.error"></a>
### `amount_details.error`

The `amount_details.error` attribute supports:

* `code` - The code of the error that occurred when validating the current amount details. Possible values: `amount_details_amount_mismatch`, `amount_details_tax_shipping_discount_greater_than_amount`.
* `message` - A message providing more details about the error.

<a id="amount_details.shipping"></a>
### `amount_details.shipping`

The `amount_details.shipping` attribute supports:

* `amount` - (Optional) If a physical good is being shipped, the cost of shipping represented in the [smallest currency unit](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies#zero-decimal). An integer greater than or equal to 0. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `from_postal_code` - (Optional) If a physical good is being shipped, the postal code of where it is being shipped from. At most 10 alphanumeric characters long, hyphens and spaces are allowed. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `to_postal_code` - (Optional) If a physical good is being shipped, the postal code of where it is being shipped to. At most 10 alphanumeric characters long, hyphens and spaces are allowed. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.

<a id="amount_details.tax"></a>
### `amount_details.tax`

The `amount_details.tax` attribute supports:

* `total_tax_amount` - (Required) The total amount of tax on the transaction represented in the [smallest currency unit](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies#zero-decimal). Required for L2 rates. An integer greater than or equal to 0. This field is mutually exclusive with the `amount_details[line_items][#][tax][total_tax_amount]` field.

<a id="automatic_payment_methods"></a>
### `automatic_payment_methods`

The `automatic_payment_methods` attribute supports:

* `allow_redirects` - (Optional) Controls whether this PaymentIntent will accept redirect-based payment methods. Redirect-based payment methods may require your customer to be redirected to a payment method's app or site for authentication or additional steps. To [confirm](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_intents/confirm) this PaymentIntent, you may be required to provide a `return_url` to redirect customers back to your site after they authenticate or complete the payment. Possible values: `always`, `never`. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `enabled` - (Required) Automatically calculates compatible payment methods

<a id="hooks"></a>
### `hooks`

The `hooks` attribute supports:

* `inputs` - (Optional) Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value. See [`hooks.inputs`](#hooks.inputs) below.

<a id="hooks.inputs"></a>
### `hooks.inputs`

The `hooks.inputs` attribute supports:

* `tax` - (Optional) Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value. See [`hooks.inputs.tax`](#hooks.inputs.tax) below.

<a id="hooks.inputs.tax"></a>
### `hooks.inputs.tax`

The `hooks.inputs.tax` attribute supports:

* `calculation` - (Required) The [TaxCalculation](https://docs.stripe.com/api/tax/calculations) id. Stripe refused it on a US account on create and update: "You must provide an existing Tax Calculation ID, see https://docs.stripe.com/tax/custom#calculate-tax for information on how to calculate tax.".

<a id="payment_details"></a>
### `payment_details`

The `payment_details` attribute supports:

* `customer_reference` - (Optional) A unique value to identify the customer. This field is available only for card payments. This field is truncated to 25 alphanumeric characters, excluding spaces, before being sent to card networks. Default: none.
* `order_reference` - (Optional) A unique value assigned by the business to identify the transaction. Required for L2 and L3 rates. For Cards, this field is truncated to 25 alphanumeric characters, excluding spaces, before being sent to card networks. For Klarna, this field is truncated to 255 characters and is visible to customers when they view the order in the Klarna app. Default: none.

<a id="payment_method_options.acss_debit"></a>
### `payment_method_options.acss_debit`

The `payment_method_options.acss_debit` attribute supports:

* `mandate_options` - (Optional) Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value. See [`payment_method_options.acss_debit.mandate_options`](#payment_method_options.acss_debit.mandate_options) below.
* `setup_future_usage` - (Optional) Indicates that you intend to make future payments with this PaymentIntent's payment method. If you provide a Customer with the PaymentIntent, you can use this parameter to [attach the payment method](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/save-during-payment) to the Customer after the PaymentIntent is confirmed and the customer completes any required actions. If you don't provide a Customer, you can still [attach](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_methods/attach) the payment method to a Customer after the transaction completes. If the payment method is `card_present` and isn't a digital wallet, Stripe creates and attaches a [generated_card](https://docs.stripe.com/api/charges/object#charge_object-payment_method_details-card_present-generated_card) payment method representing the card to the Customer instead. When processing card payments, Stripe uses `setup_future_usage` to help you comply with regional legislation and network rules, such as [SCA](https://docs.stripe.com/strong-customer-authentication). Possible values: `none`, `off_session`, `on_session`. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `target_date` - (Optional) Controls when Stripe will attempt to debit the funds from the customer's account. The date must be a string in YYYY-MM-DD format. The date must be in the future and between 3 and 15 calendar days from now. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `verification_method` - (Optional) Bank account verification method. The default value is `automatic`. Possible values: `automatic`, `instant`, `microdeposits`. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.

<a id="payment_method_options.acss_debit.mandate_options"></a>

* `custom_mandate_url` - (Optional) A URL for custom mandate text. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `interval_description` - (Optional) Description of the interval. Only required if the 'payment_schedule' parameter is 'interval' or 'combined'. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `payment_schedule` - (Optional) Payment schedule for the mandate. Possible values: `combined`, `interval`, `sporadic`. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `transaction_type` - (Optional) Transaction type of the mandate. Possible values: `business`, `personal`. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.

<a id="payment_method_options.affirm"></a>
### `payment_method_options.affirm`

The `payment_method_options.affirm` attribute supports:

* `capture_method` - (Optional) Controls when the funds will be captured from the customer's account. Possible values: `manual`. Stripe fails an update that unsets it on every attempt, so the provider sends no unset of its own: removing it from the configuration leaves it out of the hash the update sends ("Stripe answers 500 to an update that sends `payment_method_options[affirm][capture_method]=` (dev records, 2026-11-07); Afterpay takes the same unset"). Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `preferred_locale` - (Optional) Preferred language of the Affirm authorization page that the customer is redirected to. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `setup_future_usage` - (Optional) Indicates that you intend to make future payments with this PaymentIntent's payment method. When processing card payments, Stripe uses `setup_future_usage` to help you comply with regional legislation and network rules, such as [SCA](https://docs.stripe.com/strong-customer-authentication). Possible values: `none`. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.

<a id="payment_method_options.card"></a>
### `payment_method_options.card`

The `payment_method_options.card` attribute supports:

* `capture_method` - (Optional) Controls when the funds will be captured from the customer's account. Possible values: `manual`. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `cvc_token` - (Optional) Stripe refused it on a US account on create: "No such cvc_update: 'cvctok_...'". Stripe refused it on a US account on update: "The parameter `payment_method_options[card][cvc_token]` cannot be used when creating a PaymentIntent unless `confirm` is set to true.".
* `installments` - (Optional) Stripe does not return this value; the provider keeps it from configuration. See [`payment_method_options.card.installments`](#payment_method_options.card.installments) below.
* `mandate_options` - (Optional) Configuration options for setting up an eMandate for cards issued in India. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value. See [`payment_method_options.card.mandate_options`](#payment_method_options.card.mandate_options) below.
* `network` - (Optional) Selected network to process this payment intent on. Depends on the available networks of the card attached to the payment intent. Can be only set confirm-time. Possible values: `amex`, `cartes_bancaires`, `diners`, `discover`, `eftpos_au`, `girocard`, `interac`, `jcb`, `link`, `mastercard`, `unionpay`, `unknown`, `visa`. Stripe refused it on a US account on update: "The parameter `payment_method_options[card][network]` cannot be used when creating a PaymentIntent unless `confirm` is set to true.". Default: not sent. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `request_extended_authorization` - (Optional) Request ability to [capture beyond the standard authorization validity window](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/extended-authorization) for this PaymentIntent. Possible values: `if_available`, `never`. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `request_incremental_authorization` - (Optional) Request ability to [increment the authorization](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/incremental-authorization) for this PaymentIntent. Possible values: `if_available`, `never`. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `request_multicapture` - (Optional) Possible values: `if_available`, `never`. Stripe does not return this value; the provider keeps it from configuration.
* `request_overcapture` - (Optional) Request ability to [overcapture](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/overcapture) for this PaymentIntent. Possible values: `if_available`, `never`. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `request_three_d_secure` - (Optional) We strongly recommend that you rely on our SCA Engine to automatically prompt your customers for authentication based on risk level and [other requirements](https://docs.stripe.com/strong-customer-authentication). However, if you wish to request 3D Secure based on logic from your own fraud engine, provide this option. If not provided, this value defaults to `automatic`. Read our guide on [manually requesting 3D Secure](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/3d-secure/authentication-flow#manual-three-ds) for more information on how this configuration interacts with Radar and our SCA Engine. Possible values: `any`, `automatic`, `challenge`. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `require_cvc_recollection` - (Optional) When enabled, using a card that is attached to a customer will require the CVC to be provided again (i.e. using the cvc_token parameter). Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `setup_future_usage` - (Optional) Indicates that you intend to make future payments with this PaymentIntent's payment method. If you provide a Customer with the PaymentIntent, you can use this parameter to [attach the payment method](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/save-during-payment) to the Customer after the PaymentIntent is confirmed and the customer completes any required actions. If you don't provide a Customer, you can still [attach](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_methods/attach) the payment method to a Customer after the transaction completes. If the payment method is `card_present` and isn't a digital wallet, Stripe creates and attaches a [generated_card](https://docs.stripe.com/api/charges/object#charge_object-payment_method_details-card_present-generated_card) payment method representing the card to the Customer instead. When processing card payments, Stripe uses `setup_future_usage` to help you comply with regional legislation and network rules, such as [SCA](https://docs.stripe.com/strong-customer-authentication). Possible values: `none`, `off_session`, `on_session`. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `statement_descriptor_suffix_kana` - (Optional) Stripe does not return this value; the provider keeps it from configuration.
* `statement_descriptor_suffix_kanji` - (Optional) Stripe does not return this value; the provider keeps it from configuration.

<a id="payment_method_options.card.installments"></a>
### `payment_method_options.card.installments`

The `payment_method_options.card.installments` attribute supports:

* `enabled` - (Optional) Stripe does not return this value; the provider keeps it from configuration.

<a id="payment_method_options.card.mandate_options"></a>
### `payment_method_options.card.mandate_options`

The `payment_method_options.card.mandate_options` attribute supports:

* `amount` - (Required) Amount to be charged for future payments, specified in the presentment currency.
* `amount_type` - (Required) One of `fixed` or `maximum`. If `fixed`, the `amount` param refers to the exact amount to be charged in future payments. If `maximum`, the amount charged can be up to the value passed for the `amount` param. Possible values: `fixed`, `maximum`.
* `description` - (Optional) A description of the mandate or subscription that is meant to be displayed to the customer. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `end_date` - (Optional) End date of the mandate or subscription. If not provided, the mandate will be active until canceled. If provided, end date should be after start date. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `interval` - (Required) Specifies payment frequency. One of `day`, `week`, `month`, `year`, or `sporadic`. Possible values: `day`, `month`, `sporadic`, `week`, `year`.
* `interval_count` - (Optional) The number of intervals between payments. For example, `interval=month` and `interval_count=3` indicates one payment every three months. Maximum of one year interval allowed (1 year, 12 months, or 52 weeks). This parameter is optional when `interval=sporadic`. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `reference` - (Required) Unique identifier for the mandate or subscription.
* `start_date` - (Required) Start date of the mandate or subscription. Start date should not be lesser than yesterday.
* `supported_types` - (Optional) Specifies the type of mandates supported. Possible values are `india`. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.

<a id="payment_method_options.card_present"></a>
### `payment_method_options.card_present`

The `payment_method_options.card_present` attribute supports:

* `capture_method` - (Optional) Controls when the funds will be captured from the customer's account. Possible values: `manual`, `manual_preferred`. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `request_extended_authorization` - (Optional) Request ability to capture this payment beyond the standard [authorization validity window](https://docs.stripe.com/terminal/features/extended-authorizations#authorization-validity). Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `request_incremental_authorization_support` - (Optional) Request ability to [increment](https://docs.stripe.com/terminal/features/incremental-authorizations) this PaymentIntent if the combination of MCC and card brand is eligible. Check [incremental_authorization_supported](https://docs.stripe.com/api/charges/object#charge_object-payment_method_details-card_present-incremental_authorization_supported) in the [Confirm](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_intents/confirm) response to verify support. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `routing` - (Optional) See [`payment_method_options.card_present.routing`](#payment_method_options.card_present.routing) below.

<a id="payment_method_options.pix.mandate_options"></a>
### `payment_method_options.pix.mandate_options`

The `payment_method_options.pix.mandate_options` attribute supports:

* `amount` - (Optional) Amount to be charged for future payments. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `amount_includes_iof` - (Optional) Determines if the amount includes the IOF tax. Possible values: `always`, `never`. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `amount_type` - (Optional) Type of amount. Possible values: `fixed`, `maximum`. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `currency` - (Optional) Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `end_date` - (Optional) Date when the mandate expires and no further payments will be charged, in `YYYY-MM-DD`. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `payment_schedule` - (Optional) Schedule at which the future payments will be charged. Possible values: `halfyearly`, `monthly`, `quarterly`, `weekly`, `yearly`. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `reference` - (Optional) Subscription name displayed to buyers in their bank app. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `start_date` - (Optional) Start date of the mandate, in `YYYY-MM-DD`. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.

<a id="payment_method_options.upi"></a>
### `payment_method_options.upi`

The `payment_method_options.upi` attribute supports:

* `mandate_options` - (Optional) Stripe does not return this value; the provider keeps it from configuration. See [`payment_method_options.upi.mandate_options`](#payment_method_options.upi.mandate_options) below.
* `setup_future_usage` - (Optional) Indicates that you intend to make future payments with this PaymentIntent's payment method. If you provide a Customer with the PaymentIntent, you can use this parameter to [attach the payment method](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/save-during-payment) to the Customer after the PaymentIntent is confirmed and the customer completes any required actions. If you don't provide a Customer, you can still [attach](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_methods/attach) the payment method to a Customer after the transaction completes. If the payment method is `card_present` and isn't a digital wallet, Stripe creates and attaches a [generated_card](https://docs.stripe.com/api/charges/object#charge_object-payment_method_details-card_present-generated_card) payment method representing the card to the Customer instead. When processing card payments, Stripe uses `setup_future_usage` to help you comply with regional legislation and network rules, such as [SCA](https://docs.stripe.com/strong-customer-authentication). Possible values: `none`, `off_session`, `on_session`. Stripe fails an update that unsets it on every attempt, so the provider sends no unset of its own: removing it from the configuration leaves it out of the hash the update sends ("Stripe answers 500 to an update that sends `payment_method_options[upi][setup_future_usage]=` alone (dev records, 2026-11-07); every other method whose spec offers `\"\"` there takes it, and a method whose spec does not refuses it as `cannot be unset`"). Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.

* `target_date` - (Optional) Controls when Stripe will attempt to debit the funds from the customer's account. The date must be a string in YYYY-MM-DD format. The date must be in the future and between 3 and 15 calendar days from now. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `transaction_purpose` - (Optional) The purpose of the transaction. Possible values: `goods`, `other`, `services`, `unspecified`. Stripe fails an update that unsets it on every attempt, so the provider sends no unset of its own: removing it from the configuration leaves it out of the hash the update sends ("Stripe answers 500 to an update that sends `payment_method_options[us_bank_account][transaction_purpose]=` beside the hash's shortened lists and `mandate_options[collection_method]=` (req_FAu6kee5xSV15l); an update sends those lists whole and `collection_method=` and is answered, and a prefetch its permissions do not cover is refused with a 400"). Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `verification_method` - (Optional) Bank account verification method. The default value is `automatic`. Possible values: `automatic`, `instant`, `microdeposits`. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.

<a id="payment_method_options.us_bank_account.financial_connections"></a>
### `payment_method_options.us_bank_account.financial_connections`

The `payment_method_options.us_bank_account.financial_connections` attribute supports:

* `filters` - (Optional) Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value. See [`payment_method_options.us_bank_account.financial_connections.filters`](#payment_method_options.us_bank_account.financial_connections.filters) below.
* `permissions` - (Optional) The list of permissions to request. The `payment_method` permission must be included. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `prefetch` - (Optional) Data features requested to be retrieved upon account creation. Stripe refused it on a US account on update: "You do not have the required permissions to prefetch.". Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `return_url` - (Optional) For webview integrations only. Upon completing OAuth login in the native browser, the user will be redirected to this URL to return to your app. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.

<a id="payment_method_options.us_bank_account.financial_connections.filters"></a>
### `payment_method_options.us_bank_account.financial_connections.filters`

The `payment_method_options.us_bank_account.financial_connections.filters` attribute supports:

* `account_subcategories` - (Optional) The account subcategories to use to filter for possible accounts to link. Valid subcategories are `checking` and `savings`. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.

<a id="payment_method_options.us_bank_account.mandate_options"></a>
### `payment_method_options.us_bank_account.mandate_options`

The `payment_method_options.us_bank_account.mandate_options` attribute supports:

* `collection_method` - (Optional) Mandate collection method Possible values: `paper`. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.

<a id="payment_method_options.us_bank_account.networks"></a>
### `payment_method_options.us_bank_account.networks`

The `payment_method_options.us_bank_account.networks` attribute supports:

* `requested` - (Optional) Stripe does not return this value; the provider keeps it from configuration.

<a id="payment_method_options.wechat_pay"></a>
### `payment_method_options.wechat_pay`

The `payment_method_options.wechat_pay` attribute supports:

* `app_id` - (Optional) The app ID registered with WeChat Pay. Only required when client is ios, android, or mini_program. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `client` - (Optional) The client type that the end customer will pay from Possible values: `android`, `ios`, `web`. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `setup_future_usage` - (Optional) Indicates that you intend to make future payments with this PaymentIntent's payment method. If you provide a Customer with the PaymentIntent, you can use this parameter to [attach the payment method](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/save-during-payment) to the Customer after the PaymentIntent is confirmed and the customer completes any required actions. If you don't provide a Customer, you can still [attach](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_methods/attach) the payment method to a Customer after the transaction completes. If the payment method is `card_present` and isn't a digital wallet, Stripe creates and attaches a [generated_card](https://docs.stripe.com/api/charges/object#charge_object-payment_method_details-card_present-generated_card) payment method representing the card to the Customer instead. When processing card payments, Stripe uses `setup_future_usage` to help you comply with regional legislation and network rules, such as [SCA](https://docs.stripe.com/strong-customer-authentication). Possible values: `none`. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.

<a id="radar_options"></a>
### `radar_options`

The `radar_options` attribute supports:

* `session` - (Optional) Stripe refused it on a US account on create: "No such radar session: 'rse_...'".

<a id="shipping"></a>
### `shipping`

The `shipping` attribute supports:

* `address` - (Required) See [`shipping.address`](#shipping.address) below.
* `carrier` - (Optional) The delivery service that shipped a physical product, such as Fedex, UPS, USPS, etc. Default: none.
* `name` - (Required) Recipient name.
* `phone` - (Optional) Recipient phone (including extension). Default: none.
* `tracking_number` - (Optional) The tracking number for a physical product, obtained from the delivery service. If multiple tracking numbers were generated for this purchase, please separate them with commas. Default: none.

<a id="shipping.address"></a>
### `shipping.address`

The `shipping.address` attribute supports:

* `city` - (Optional) City, district, suburb, town, or village. Default: none.
* `country` - (Optional) Two-letter country code ([ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2)). Default: none.
* `line1` - (Optional) Address line 1, such as the street, PO Box, or company name. Default: none.
* `line2` - (Optional) Address line 2, such as the apartment, suite, unit, or building. Default: none.
* `postal_code` - (Optional) ZIP or postal code. Default: none.
* `state` - (Optional) State, county, province, or region ([ISO 3166-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-2)). Default: none.

<a id="transfer_data"></a>
### `transfer_data`

The `transfer_data` attribute supports:

* `amount` - (Optional) The amount transferred to the destination account. This transfer will occur automatically after the payment succeeds. If no amount is specified, by default the entire payment amount is transferred to the destination account. The amount must be less than or equal to the [amount](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_intents/object#payment_intent_object-amount), and must be a positive integer representing how much to transfer in the smallest currency unit (e.g., 100 cents to charge $1.00). Default: none.
* `description` - (Optional) An arbitrary string attached to the transfer. Often useful for displaying to users. Default: none.
* `destination` - (Required) The account (if any) that the payment is attributed to for tax reporting, and where funds from the payment are transferred to after payment success. Changing it fails the plan, because this resource cannot be replaced.
* `metadata` - (Optional) Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Default: none.
* `payment_data` - (Optional) See [`transfer_data.payment_data`](#transfer_data.payment_data) below.

<a id="transfer_data.payment_data"></a>
### `transfer_data.payment_data`

The `transfer_data.payment_data` attribute supports:

* `description` - (Optional) An arbitrary string attached to the destination payment. Often useful for displaying to users. Default: none.
* `metadata` - (Optional) Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Default: none.

## Attribute Reference

This resource exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `amount_capturable` - Amount that can be captured from this PaymentIntent.
* `amount_received` - Amount that this PaymentIntent collects.
* `application` - ID of the Connect application that created the PaymentIntent.
* `canceled_at` - Populated when `status` is `canceled`, this is the time at which the PaymentIntent was canceled. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `cancellation_reason` - Reason for cancellation of this PaymentIntent, either user-provided (`duplicate`, `fraudulent`, `requested_by_customer`, or `abandoned`) or generated by Stripe internally (`failed_invoice`, `void_invoice`, `automatic`, or `expired`). Possible values: `abandoned`, `automatic`, `duplicate`, `expired`, `failed_invoice`, `fraudulent`, `requested_by_customer`, `void_invoice`.
* `client_secret` - (Sensitive) The client secret of this PaymentIntent. Used for client-side retrieval using a publishable key. The client secret can be used to complete a payment from your frontend. It should not be stored, logged, or exposed to anyone other than the customer. Make sure that you have TLS enabled on any page that includes the client secret. Refer to our docs to [accept a payment](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/accept-a-payment?ui=elements) and learn about how `client_secret` should be handled.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `last_payment_error` - The payment error encountered in the previous PaymentIntent confirmation. It will be cleared if the PaymentIntent is later updated for any reason. See [`last_payment_error`](#last_payment_error) below.
* `latest_charge` - ID of the latest [Charge object](https://docs.stripe.com/api/charges) created by this PaymentIntent. This property is `null` until PaymentIntent confirmation is attempted.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `managed_payments` - Settings for Managed Payments. See [`managed_payments`](#managed_payments) below.
* `next_action` - If present, this property tells you what actions you need to take in order for your customer to fulfill a payment using the provided source. See [`next_action`](#next_action) below.
* `payment_method_configuration_details` - Information about the [payment method configuration](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_method_configurations) used for this PaymentIntent. See [`payment_method_configuration_details`](#payment_method_configuration_details) below.
* `payment_method_types` - The list of payment method types (e.g. card) that this PaymentIntent is allowed to use. A comprehensive list of valid payment method types can be found [here](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_methods/object#payment_method_object-type).
* `payment_record` - ID of the [Payment Record object](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment-record) created by this PaymentIntent.
* `presentment_details` - See [`presentment_details`](#presentment_details) below.
* `processing` - If present, this property tells you about the processing state of the payment. See [`processing`](#processing) below.
* `review` - ID of the review associated with this PaymentIntent, if any.

<a id="last_payment_error"></a>
### `last_payment_error`

The `last_payment_error` attribute supports:

* `advice_code` - For card errors resulting from a card issuer decline, a short string indicating [how to proceed with an error](https://docs.stripe.com/declines/card#retrying-issuer-declines) if they provide one.
* `charge` - For card errors, the ID of the failed charge.
* `code` - For some errors that could be handled programmatically, a short string indicating the [error code](https://docs.stripe.com/error-codes) reported.
* `decline_code` - For card errors resulting from a card issuer decline, a short string indicating the [card issuer's reason for the decline](https://docs.stripe.com/declines#issuer-declines) if they provide one.
* `doc_url` - A URL to more information about the [error code](https://docs.stripe.com/error-codes) reported.
* `message` - A human-readable message providing more details about the error. For card errors, these messages can be shown to your users.
* `network_advice_code` - For card errors resulting from a card issuer decline, a 2 digit code which indicates the advice given to merchant by the card network on how to proceed with an error.
* `network_decline_code` - For payments declined by the network, an alphanumeric code which indicates the reason the payment failed.
* `param` - If the error is parameter-specific, the parameter related to the error. For example, you can use this to display a message near the correct form field.
* `payment_method` - PaymentMethod objects represent your customer's payment instruments. You can use them with [PaymentIntents](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-intents) to collect payments or save them to Customer objects to store instrument details for future payments. Related guides: [Payment Methods](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-methods) and [More Payment Scenarios](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/more-payment-scenarios). See [`last_payment_error.payment_method`](#last_payment_error.payment_method) below.
* `payment_method_type` - If the error is specific to the type of payment method, the payment method type that had a problem. This field is only populated for invoice-related errors.
* `request_log_url` - A URL to the request log entry in your dashboard.
* `setup_intent` - A SetupIntent guides you through the process of setting up and saving a customer's payment credentials for future payments. For example, you can use a SetupIntent to set up and save your customer's card without immediately collecting a payment. Later, you can use [PaymentIntents](https://docs.stripe.com/api#payment_intents) to drive the payment flow. Create a SetupIntent when you're ready to collect your customer's payment credentials. Don't maintain long-lived, unconfirmed SetupIntents because they might not be valid. The SetupIntent transitions through multiple [statuses](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/intents#intent-statuses) as it guides you through the setup process. Successful SetupIntents result in payment credentials that are optimized for future payments. For example, cardholders in [certain regions](https://stripe.com/guides/strong-customer-authentication) might need to be run through [Strong Customer Authentication](https://docs.stripe.com/strong-customer-authentication) during payment method collection to streamline later [off-session payments](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/setup-intents). If you use the SetupIntent with a [Customer](https://docs.stripe.com/api#setup_intent_object-customer), it automatically attaches the resulting payment method to that Customer after successful setup. We recommend using SetupIntents or [setup_future_usage](https://docs.stripe.com/api#payment_intent_object-setup_future_usage) on PaymentIntents to save payment methods to prevent saving invalid or unoptimized payment methods. By using SetupIntents, you can reduce friction for your customers, even as regulations change over time. Related guide: [Setup Intents API](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/setup-intents) See [`last_payment_error.setup_intent`](#last_payment_error.setup_intent) below.
* `source` - The [source object](https://docs.stripe.com/api/sources/object) for errors returned on a request involving a source. See [`last_payment_error.source`](#last_payment_error.source) below.
* `type` - The type of error returned. One of `api_error`, `card_error`, `idempotency_error`, or `invalid_request_error` Possible values: `api_error`, `card_error`, `idempotency_error`, `invalid_request_error`.

<a id="last_payment_error.payment_method"></a>
### `last_payment_error.payment_method`

The `last_payment_error.payment_method` attribute holds a customer payment method, with the attributes of the [`stripe_customer_payment_method`](../data-sources/customer_payment_method) data source and `object`, the name of its type.

<a id="last_payment_error.setup_intent"></a>
### `last_payment_error.setup_intent`

The `last_payment_error.setup_intent` attribute supports:

* `allowed_payment_method_types` - The list of payment method types to allow for this SetupIntent. Stripe will only use methods in this list when determining the payment methods to offer.
* `application` - ID of the Connect application that created the SetupIntent.
* `attach_to_self` - If present, the SetupIntent's payment method will be attached to the in-context Stripe Account. It can only be used for this Stripe Account’s own money movement flows like InboundTransfer and OutboundTransfers. It cannot be set to true when setting up a PaymentMethod for a Customer, and defaults to false when attaching a PaymentMethod to a Customer.
* `automatic_payment_methods` - Settings for dynamic payment methods compatible with this Setup Intent See [`last_payment_error.setup_intent.automatic_payment_methods`](#last_payment_error.setup_intent.automatic_payment_methods) below.
* `cancellation_reason` - Reason for cancellation of this SetupIntent, one of `abandoned`, `requested_by_customer`, or `duplicate`. Possible values: `abandoned`, `duplicate`, `requested_by_customer`.
* `client_secret` - The client secret of this SetupIntent. Used for client-side retrieval using a publishable key. The client secret can be used to complete payment setup from your frontend. It should not be stored, logged, or exposed to anyone other than the customer. Make sure that you have TLS enabled on any page that includes the client secret.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `customer` - ID of the Customer this SetupIntent belongs to, if one exists. If present, the SetupIntent's payment method will be attached to the Customer on successful setup. Payment methods attached to other Customers cannot be used with this SetupIntent.
* `customer_account` - ID of the Account this SetupIntent belongs to, if one exists. If present, the SetupIntent's payment method will be attached to the Account on successful setup. Payment methods attached to other Accounts cannot be used with this SetupIntent.
* `description` - An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.
* `excluded_payment_method_types` - Payment method types that are excluded from this SetupIntent.
* `flow_directions` - Indicates the directions of money movement for which this payment method is intended to be used. Include `inbound` if you intend to use the payment method as the origin to pull funds from. Include `outbound` if you intend to use the payment method as the destination to send funds to. You can include both if you intend to use the payment method for both purposes.
* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `latest_attempt` - The most recent SetupAttempt for this SetupIntent.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `managed_payments` - See [`last_payment_error.setup_intent.managed_payments`](#last_payment_error.setup_intent.managed_payments) below.
* `mandate` - ID of the multi use Mandate generated by the SetupIntent.
* `metadata` - Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.
* `next_action` - If present, this property tells you what actions you need to take in order for your customer to continue payment setup. See [`last_payment_error.setup_intent.next_action`](#last_payment_error.setup_intent.next_action) below.
* `object` - String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Possible values: `setup_intent`.
* `on_behalf_of` - The account (if any) for which the setup is intended.
* `payment_method` - ID of the payment method used with this SetupIntent. If the payment method is `card_present` and isn't a digital wallet, then the [generated_card](https://docs.stripe.com/api/setup_attempts/object#setup_attempt_object-payment_method_details-card_present-generated_card) associated with the `latest_attempt` is attached to the Customer instead.
* `payment_method_configuration_details` - Information about the [payment method configuration](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_method_configurations) used for this Setup Intent. See [`last_payment_error.setup_intent.payment_method_configuration_details`](#last_payment_error.setup_intent.payment_method_configuration_details) below.
* `payment_method_options` - Payment method-specific configuration for this SetupIntent. See [`last_payment_error.setup_intent.payment_method_options`](#last_payment_error.setup_intent.payment_method_options) below.
* `payment_method_types` - The list of payment method types (e.g. card) that this SetupIntent is allowed to set up. A list of valid payment method types can be found [here](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_methods/object#payment_method_object-type).
* `single_use_mandate` - ID of the single_use Mandate generated by the SetupIntent.
* `status` - [Status](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/intents#intent-statuses) of this SetupIntent, one of `requires_payment_method`, `requires_confirmation`, `requires_action`, `processing`, `canceled`, or `succeeded`. Possible values: `canceled`, `processing`, `requires_action`, `requires_confirmation`, `requires_payment_method`, `succeeded`.
* `usage` - Indicates how the payment method is intended to be used in the future. Use `on_session` if you intend to only reuse the payment method when the customer is in your checkout flow. Use `off_session` if your customer may or may not be in your checkout flow. If not provided, this value defaults to `off_session`.

<a id="last_payment_error.setup_intent.automatic_payment_methods"></a>
### `last_payment_error.setup_intent.automatic_payment_methods`

The `last_payment_error.setup_intent.automatic_payment_methods` attribute supports:

* `allow_redirects` - Controls whether this SetupIntent will accept redirect-based payment methods. Redirect-based payment methods may require your customer to be redirected to a payment method's app or site for authentication or additional steps. To [confirm](https://docs.stripe.com/api/setup_intents/confirm) this SetupIntent, you may be required to provide a `return_url` to redirect customers back to your site after they authenticate or complete the setup. Possible values: `always`, `never`.
* `enabled` - Automatically calculates compatible payment methods

<a id="last_payment_error.setup_intent.managed_payments"></a>
### `last_payment_error.setup_intent.managed_payments`

The `last_payment_error.setup_intent.managed_payments` attribute supports:

* `enabled` - Set to `true` to enable [Managed Payments](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/managed-payments), Stripe's merchant of record solution, for this session.

<a id="last_payment_error.setup_intent.next_action"></a>
### `last_payment_error.setup_intent.next_action`

The `last_payment_error.setup_intent.next_action` attribute supports:

* `cashapp_handle_redirect_or_display_qr_code` - See [`last_payment_error.setup_intent.next_action.cashapp_handle_redirect_or_display_qr_code`](#last_payment_error.setup_intent.next_action.cashapp_handle_redirect_or_display_qr_code) below.
* `pix_display_qr_code` - See [`last_payment_error.setup_intent.next_action.pix_display_qr_code`](#last_payment_error.setup_intent.next_action.pix_display_qr_code) below.
* `redirect_to_url` - See [`last_payment_error.setup_intent.next_action.redirect_to_url`](#last_payment_error.setup_intent.next_action.redirect_to_url) below.
* `type` - Type of the next action to perform. Refer to the other child attributes under `next_action` for available values. Examples include: `redirect_to_url`, `use_stripe_sdk`, `alipay_handle_redirect`, `oxxo_display_details`, or `verify_with_microdeposits`.
* `upi_handle_redirect_or_display_qr_code` - See [`last_payment_error.setup_intent.next_action.upi_handle_redirect_or_display_qr_code`](#last_payment_error.setup_intent.next_action.upi_handle_redirect_or_display_qr_code) below.
* `verify_with_microdeposits` - See [`last_payment_error.setup_intent.next_action.verify_with_microdeposits`](#last_payment_error.setup_intent.next_action.verify_with_microdeposits) below.

<a id="last_payment_error.setup_intent.next_action.cashapp_handle_redirect_or_display_qr_code"></a>
### `last_payment_error.setup_intent.next_action.cashapp_handle_redirect_or_display_qr_code`

The `last_payment_error.setup_intent.next_action.cashapp_handle_redirect_or_display_qr_code` attribute supports:

* `hosted_instructions_url` - The URL to the hosted Cash App Pay instructions page, which allows customers to view the QR code, and supports QR code refreshing on expiration.
* `mobile_auth_url` - The url for mobile redirect based auth
* `qr_code` - See [`last_payment_error.setup_intent.next_action.cashapp_handle_redirect_or_display_qr_code.qr_code`](#last_payment_error.setup_intent.next_action.cashapp_handle_redirect_or_display_qr_code.qr_code) below.

<a id="last_payment_error.setup_intent.next_action.cashapp_handle_redirect_or_display_qr_code.qr_code"></a>
### `last_payment_error.setup_intent.next_action.cashapp_handle_redirect_or_display_qr_code.qr_code`

The `last_payment_error.setup_intent.next_action.cashapp_handle_redirect_or_display_qr_code.qr_code` attribute supports:

* `expires_at` - The date (unix timestamp) when the QR code expires.
* `image_url_png` - The image_url_png string used to render QR code
* `image_url_svg` - The image_url_svg string used to render QR code

<a id="last_payment_error.setup_intent.next_action.pix_display_qr_code"></a>
### `last_payment_error.setup_intent.next_action.pix_display_qr_code`

The `last_payment_error.setup_intent.next_action.pix_display_qr_code` attribute supports:

* `data` - The raw data string used to generate QR code, it should be used together with QR code library.
* `expires_at` - The date (unix timestamp) when the PIX expires.
* `hosted_instructions_url` - The URL to the hosted pix instructions page, which allows customers to view the pix QR code.
* `image_url_png` - The image_url_png string used to render png QR code
* `image_url_svg` - The image_url_svg string used to render svg QR code

<a id="last_payment_error.setup_intent.next_action.redirect_to_url"></a>
### `last_payment_error.setup_intent.next_action.redirect_to_url`

The `last_payment_error.setup_intent.next_action.redirect_to_url` attribute supports:

* `return_url` - If the customer does not exit their browser while authenticating, they will be redirected to this specified URL after completion.
* `url` - The URL you must redirect your customer to in order to authenticate.

<a id="last_payment_error.setup_intent.next_action.upi_handle_redirect_or_display_qr_code"></a>
### `last_payment_error.setup_intent.next_action.upi_handle_redirect_or_display_qr_code`

The `last_payment_error.setup_intent.next_action.upi_handle_redirect_or_display_qr_code` attribute supports:

* `hosted_instructions_url` - The URL to the hosted UPI instructions page, which allows customers to view the QR code.
* `qr_code` - See [`last_payment_error.setup_intent.next_action.upi_handle_redirect_or_display_qr_code.qr_code`](#last_payment_error.setup_intent.next_action.upi_handle_redirect_or_display_qr_code.qr_code) below.

<a id="last_payment_error.setup_intent.next_action.upi_handle_redirect_or_display_qr_code.qr_code"></a>
### `last_payment_error.setup_intent.next_action.upi_handle_redirect_or_display_qr_code.qr_code`

The `last_payment_error.setup_intent.next_action.upi_handle_redirect_or_display_qr_code.qr_code` attribute supports:

* `expires_at` - The date (unix timestamp) when the QR code expires.
* `image_url_png` - The image_url_png string used to render QR code
* `image_url_svg` - The image_url_svg string used to render QR code

<a id="last_payment_error.setup_intent.next_action.verify_with_microdeposits"></a>
### `last_payment_error.setup_intent.next_action.verify_with_microdeposits`

The `last_payment_error.setup_intent.next_action.verify_with_microdeposits` attribute supports:

* `arrival_date` - The timestamp when the microdeposits are expected to land.
* `hosted_verification_url` - The URL for the hosted verification page, which allows customers to verify their bank account.
* `microdeposit_type` - The type of the microdeposit sent to the customer. Used to distinguish between different verification methods. Possible values: `amounts`, `descriptor_code`.

<a id="last_payment_error.setup_intent.payment_method_configuration_details"></a>
### `last_payment_error.setup_intent.payment_method_configuration_details`

The `last_payment_error.setup_intent.payment_method_configuration_details` attribute supports:

<a id="last_payment_error.setup_intent.payment_method_options.acss_debit"></a>
### `last_payment_error.setup_intent.payment_method_options.acss_debit`

The `last_payment_error.setup_intent.payment_method_options.acss_debit` attribute supports:

* `currency` - Currency supported by the bank account Possible values: `cad`, `usd`.
* `mandate_options` - See [`last_payment_error.setup_intent.payment_method_options.acss_debit.mandate_options`](#last_payment_error.setup_intent.payment_method_options.acss_debit.mandate_options) below.
* `verification_method` - Bank account verification method. The default value is `automatic`. Possible values: `automatic`, `instant`, `microdeposits`.

<a id="last_payment_error.setup_intent.payment_method_options.acss_debit.mandate_options"></a>
### `last_payment_error.setup_intent.payment_method_options.acss_debit.mandate_options`

The `last_payment_error.setup_intent.payment_method_options.acss_debit.mandate_options` attribute supports:

* `amount` - Amount that will be collected. It is required when `amount_type` is `fixed`.
* `amount_type` - The type of amount that will be collected. The amount charged must be exact or up to the value of `amount` param for `fixed` or `maximum` type respectively. Defaults to `maximum`. Possible values: `fixed`, `maximum`.
* `custom_mandate_url` - A URL for custom mandate text
* `default_for` - List of Stripe products where this mandate can be selected automatically.
* `end_date` - Date, in YYYY-MM-DD format, after which payments will not be collected. Defaults to no end date.
* `interval_description` - Description of the interval. Only required if the 'payment_schedule' parameter is 'interval' or 'combined'.
* `payment_schedule` - Payment schedule for the mandate. Possible values: `combined`, `interval`, `sporadic`, `adhoc`, `annual`, `daily`, `fortnightly`, `monthly`, `quarterly`, `semi_annual`, `weekly`.
* `payments_per_period` - The number of payments that will be made during a payment period. Defaults to 1 except for when `payment_schedule` is `adhoc`. In that case, it defaults to no limit.
* `purpose` - The purpose for which payments are made. Has a default value based on your merchant category code. Possible values: `dependant_support`, `government`, `loan`, `mortgage`, `other`, `pension`, `personal`, `retail`, `salary`, `tax`, `utility`.
* `start_date` - Date, in YYYY-MM-DD format, from which payments will be collected. Defaults to confirmation time.
* `transaction_type` - Transaction type of the mandate. Possible values: `business`, `personal`.

<a id="last_payment_error.setup_intent.payment_method_options.card"></a>
### `last_payment_error.setup_intent.payment_method_options.card`

The `last_payment_error.setup_intent.payment_method_options.card` attribute supports:

* `mandate_options` - Configuration options for setting up an eMandate for cards issued in India. See [`last_payment_error.setup_intent.payment_method_options.card.mandate_options`](#last_payment_error.setup_intent.payment_method_options.card.mandate_options) below.
* `network` - Selected network to process this SetupIntent on. Depends on the available networks of the card attached to the setup intent. Can be only set confirm-time. Possible values: `amex`, `cartes_bancaires`, `diners`, `discover`, `eftpos_au`, `girocard`, `interac`, `jcb`, `link`, `mastercard`, `unionpay`, `unknown`, `visa`.
* `request_three_d_secure` - We strongly recommend that you rely on our SCA Engine to automatically prompt your customers for authentication based on risk level and [other requirements](https://docs.stripe.com/strong-customer-authentication). However, if you wish to request 3D Secure based on logic from your own fraud engine, provide this option. If not provided, this value defaults to `automatic`. Read our guide on [manually requesting 3D Secure](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/3d-secure/authentication-flow#manual-three-ds) for more information on how this configuration interacts with Radar and our SCA Engine. Possible values: `any`, `automatic`, `challenge`.
* `verification_method` - Bank account verification method. The default value is `automatic`. Possible values: `automatic`, `instant`, `microdeposits`.

<a id="last_payment_error.setup_intent.payment_method_options.card.mandate_options"></a>
### `last_payment_error.setup_intent.payment_method_options.card.mandate_options`

The `last_payment_error.setup_intent.payment_method_options.card.mandate_options` attribute supports:

* `amount` - Amount to be charged for future payments, specified in the presentment currency.
* `amount_type` - One of `fixed` or `maximum`. If `fixed`, the `amount` param refers to the exact amount to be charged in future payments. If `maximum`, the amount charged can be up to the value passed for the `amount` param. Possible values: `fixed`, `maximum`.
* `currency` - Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).
* `description` - A description of the mandate or subscription that is meant to be displayed to the customer.
* `end_date` - End date of the mandate or subscription. If not provided, the mandate will be active until canceled. If provided, end date should be after start date.
* `interval` - Specifies payment frequency. One of `day`, `week`, `month`, `year`, or `sporadic`. Possible values: `day`, `month`, `sporadic`, `week`, `year`.
* `interval_count` - The number of intervals between payments. For example, `interval=month` and `interval_count=3` indicates one payment every three months. Maximum of one year interval allowed (1 year, 12 months, or 52 weeks). This parameter is optional when `interval=sporadic`.
* `payment_schedule` - The periodicity at which payments will be collected. Defaults to `adhoc`. Possible values: `adhoc`, `annual`, `daily`, `fortnightly`, `monthly`, `quarterly`, `semi_annual`, `weekly`.
* `payments_per_period` - The number of payments that will be made during a payment period. Defaults to 1 except for when `payment_schedule` is `adhoc`. In that case, it defaults to no limit.
* `purpose` - The purpose for which payments are made. Has a default value based on your merchant category code. Possible values: `dependant_support`, `government`, `loan`, `mortgage`, `other`, `pension`, `personal`, `retail`, `salary`, `tax`, `utility`.
* `reference` - Unique identifier for the mandate or subscription.
* `start_date` - Start date of the mandate or subscription. Start date should not be lesser than yesterday.
* `supported_types` - Specifies the type of mandates supported. Possible values are `india`.

### `last_payment_error.setup_intent.payment_method_options.payto.mandate_options`

The `last_payment_error.setup_intent.payment_method_options.payto.mandate_options` attribute supports:

* `amount` - Amount that will be collected. It is required when `amount_type` is `fixed`.
* `amount_type` - The type of amount that will be collected. The amount charged must be exact or up to the value of `amount` param for `fixed` or `maximum` type respectively. Defaults to `maximum`. Possible values: `fixed`, `maximum`.
* `end_date` - Date, in YYYY-MM-DD format, after which payments will not be collected. Defaults to no end date.
* `payment_schedule` - The periodicity at which payments will be collected. Defaults to `adhoc`. Possible values: `adhoc`, `annual`, `daily`, `fortnightly`, `monthly`, `quarterly`, `semi_annual`, `weekly`.
* `payments_per_period` - The number of payments that will be made during a payment period. Defaults to 1 except for when `payment_schedule` is `adhoc`. In that case, it defaults to no limit.
* `purpose` - The purpose for which payments are made. Has a default value based on your merchant category code. Possible values: `dependant_support`, `government`, `loan`, `mortgage`, `other`, `pension`, `personal`, `retail`, `salary`, `tax`, `utility`.
* `start_date` - Date, in YYYY-MM-DD format, from which payments will be collected. Defaults to confirmation time.

<a id="last_payment_error.setup_intent.payment_method_options.pix"></a>
### `last_payment_error.setup_intent.payment_method_options.pix`

The `last_payment_error.setup_intent.payment_method_options.pix` attribute supports:

* `mandate_options` - See [`last_payment_error.setup_intent.payment_method_options.pix.mandate_options`](#last_payment_error.setup_intent.payment_method_options.pix.mandate_options) below.
* `verification_method` - Bank account verification method. The default value is `automatic`. Possible values: `automatic`, `instant`, `microdeposits`.

<a id="last_payment_error.setup_intent.payment_method_options.pix.mandate_options"></a>
### `last_payment_error.setup_intent.payment_method_options.pix.mandate_options`

The `last_payment_error.setup_intent.payment_method_options.pix.mandate_options` attribute supports:

* `amount` - Amount to be charged for future payments.
* `amount_includes_iof` - Determines if the amount includes the IOF tax. Possible values: `always`, `never`.
* `amount_type` - Type of amount. Possible values: `fixed`, `maximum`.
* `currency` - Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase.
* `end_date` - Date when the mandate expires and no further payments will be charged, in `YYYY-MM-DD`.
* `payment_schedule` - Schedule at which the future payments will be charged. Possible values: `halfyearly`, `monthly`, `quarterly`, `weekly`, `yearly`, `adhoc`, `annual`, `daily`, `fortnightly`, `semi_annual`.
* `payments_per_period` - The number of payments that will be made during a payment period. Defaults to 1 except for when `payment_schedule` is `adhoc`. In that case, it defaults to no limit.
* `purpose` - The purpose for which payments are made. Has a default value based on your merchant category code. Possible values: `dependant_support`, `government`, `loan`, `mortgage`, `other`, `pension`, `personal`, `retail`, `salary`, `tax`, `utility`.
* `reference` - Subscription name displayed to buyers in their bank app.
* `start_date` - Start date of the mandate, in `YYYY-MM-DD`.

<a id="last_payment_error.setup_intent.payment_method_options.sepa_debit"></a>
### `last_payment_error.setup_intent.payment_method_options.sepa_debit`

The `last_payment_error.setup_intent.payment_method_options.sepa_debit` attribute supports:

* `mandate_options` - See [`last_payment_error.setup_intent.payment_method_options.sepa_debit.mandate_options`](#last_payment_error.setup_intent.payment_method_options.sepa_debit.mandate_options) below.
* `verification_method` - Bank account verification method. The default value is `automatic`. Possible values: `automatic`, `instant`, `microdeposits`.

<a id="last_payment_error.setup_intent.payment_method_options.sepa_debit.mandate_options"></a>
### `last_payment_error.setup_intent.payment_method_options.sepa_debit.mandate_options`

The `last_payment_error.setup_intent.payment_method_options.sepa_debit.mandate_options` attribute supports:

* `amount` - Amount that will be collected. It is required when `amount_type` is `fixed`.
* `amount_type` - The type of amount that will be collected. The amount charged must be exact or up to the value of `amount` param for `fixed` or `maximum` type respectively. Defaults to `maximum`. Possible values: `fixed`, `maximum`.
* `end_date` - Date, in YYYY-MM-DD format, after which payments will not be collected. Defaults to no end date.
* `payment_schedule` - The periodicity at which payments will be collected. Defaults to `adhoc`. Possible values: `adhoc`, `annual`, `daily`, `fortnightly`, `monthly`, `quarterly`, `semi_annual`, `weekly`.
* `payments_per_period` - The number of payments that will be made during a payment period. Defaults to 1 except for when `payment_schedule` is `adhoc`. In that case, it defaults to no limit.
* `purpose` - The purpose for which payments are made. Has a default value based on your merchant category code. Possible values: `dependant_support`, `government`, `loan`, `mortgage`, `other`, `pension`, `personal`, `retail`, `salary`, `tax`, `utility`.
* `reference_prefix` - Prefix used to generate the Mandate reference. Must be at most 12 characters long. Must consist of only uppercase letters, numbers, spaces, or the following special characters: '/', '_', '-', '&', '.'. Cannot begin with 'STRIPE'.
* `start_date` - Date, in YYYY-MM-DD format, from which payments will be collected. Defaults to confirmation time.

<a id="last_payment_error.setup_intent.payment_method_options.upi"></a>
### `last_payment_error.setup_intent.payment_method_options.upi`

The `last_payment_error.setup_intent.payment_method_options.upi` attribute supports:
